The Independent — confirmed published 1 October 2026, 12:55 BST. Author: Harriette Boucher.
Headline: "UK in emergency talks with European allies over releasing diesel stocks"

Britain and its European allies are discussing tapping into emergency stockpiles of diesel after Donald Trump threatened a ban on US exports. Officials from the UK, Germany, France, Italy and Ireland held calls on Thursday morning to discuss the possible need to release their emergency stocks.

Trump had reportedly told Germany and France to draw down emergency diesel inventories to help ease global fuel prices, as he threatened to cut off American supply. The US president is said to be frustrated with the two countries for not fully following through on earlier commitments to release emergency oil and petroleum stocks. His ongoing war with Iran, along with the Russia-Ukraine conflict, continues to choke off global oil supplies.

QUOTE (unnamed US official, to Reuters): "It is in Europe's best interest to work with the United States as we pursue multiple pathways to boost the supply of refined products and lower costs for consumers."

QUOTE (Chris Wright, US Energy Secretary, to reporters on Wednesday): "We've lost some diesel exports from the Middle East, although we're restoring those, and we've lost diesel exports from China. So that's a lot of interruptions."
He said the US administration expected announcements soon from Europe about new diesel supplies.
